text:
Recommended protocol, synthesized from the sources: compare baseline SASRec, an ungated residual, a scale-matched constant gate, and the adaptive gate. Copy identical backbone weights; initialize corresponding residual branches identically. Match minibatches, sampled training negatives, and backbone dropout randomness using separate RNG streams so added parameters cannot shift baseline randomness. Keep preprocessing seed=0 and training seed=42. Define constant-gate scaling before validation, using training-only residual-to-backbone RMS; report achieved scales and gate distributions. These controls distinguish adaptive gating from extra capacity and residual magnitude. [PyTorch reproducibility](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/docs/source/notes/randomness.md) supports explicit RNG management.

Predeclare GPU-second allocations within 43,200 seconds, charging diagnostics and failures; give variants equal tuning opportunities and checkpoint evaluation schedules. Report matched-step comparisons alongside equal-compute outcomes. Use the same checkpoint-selection rule and deterministic tie-breaking for every variant; report a prespecified final checkpoint alongside validation-selected results. Repeated checkpoint/configuration selection can overfit validation, so winning validation scores are exploratory evidence, not unbiased confirmation. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html). Preserve the pinned 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed=42. Sampled HR@10 need not preserve full-catalog model rankings. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

Save paired per-user hit differences; bootstrap users within each dataset, preserving model pairing, then equally average the four dataset differences. Report dataset deltas and a macro-delta confidence interval, explicitly conditional on trained checkpoints and fixed candidates; this excludes training-seed variability and selection bias. [Benchmark variance study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03098). Before accepting results, compare in-memory and exported predictors on identical histories/candidates: scores, rankings, padding, truncation, routing, and checkpoint loading. Require evaluation mode and update the predictor writer. [PyTorch inference guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models.html).
